title: Machine Learning, AI, and LLM Capability Map
description: A coverage baseline to prune and reorder after diagnostic evidence; not a fixed linear course.

included: classical artificial intelligence and machine learning
LLM application engineering, evaluation, security, and operations
research reading, replication, and integrated capability
excluded: domain-specialist computer vision and speech systems

llm-application-builder: Build and evaluate a grounded LLM application with typed tools, representative evals, and explicit security boundaries.
ml-engineer: Frame, train, evaluate, debug, and operate a reproducible machine-learning system against a real decision objective.
ai-systems-builder: Model and implement search, inference, planning, learning, and evaluation components for a bounded artificial-intelligence system.
llm-engineer: Explain and implement the major model and systems mechanisms behind a reliable language-model product.
research: Read, reproduce, challenge, and defend a scoped machine-learning or language-model research result with appropriate controls.

sources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
sources.organization: Dive into Deep Learning authors and contributors
sources.authority: Maintained technical textbook with executable examples
sources.license_reuse: Link and paraphrase; verify the edition's stated license before redistributing text, figures, or code.
sources.known_gaps: Broad treatment; use original papers and framework documentation for fast-moving implementation details.

sources.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
sources.authority: Widely used statistical-learning textbook maintained by its authors
sources.license_reuse: Free access does not imply open redistribution; link and paraphrase unless publisher terms explicitly allow reuse.
sources.known_gaps: Emphasizes statistical learning rather than production systems or modern foundation models.

sources.title: scikit-learn User Guide
sources.authority: Official maintained documentation for the referenced library
sources.license_reuse: Link to canonical documentation; verify project BSD licensing and documentation terms before redistribution.
sources.known_gaps: Library-specific guidance is not a substitute for statistical assumptions or deployment design.

sources.title: PyTorch Tutorials
sources.license_reuse: Link to canonical tutorials; verify current code and documentation licenses before redistribution.
sources.known_gaps: Framework examples can hide conceptual prerequisites and do not establish model validity by themselves.

sources.title: UC Berkeley CS188: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
sources.authority: Maintained university course covering classical artificial intelligence
sources.license_reuse: Link and paraphrase only unless a specific artifact states a reusable license.
sources.known_gaps: Course editions differ and do not cover every modern deep-learning or production topic.

sources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
sources.authority: Maintained course from a major open-source model tooling organization
sources.license_reuse: Link and paraphrase; verify the repository license for any copied code or media.
sources.known_gaps: Tooling-oriented examples may lag research and do not replace original papers or independent evaluation.

sources.title: Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
sources.authority: Advanced university course grounded in implementation and research literature
sources.license_reuse: Link and paraphrase; course access does not grant blanket redistribution rights.
sources.known_gaps: Advanced and compute-intensive; it assumes substantial mathematics and systems preparation.

sources.title: Full Stack Deep Learning
sources.authority: Maintained practitioner course on the deep-learning product lifecycle
sources.license_reuse: Link and paraphrase; verify each course artifact's reuse terms before redistribution.
sources.known_gaps: Practice-oriented coverage is not a substitute for primary research evidence or organization-specific controls.

sources.title: OpenAI Developer Documentation
sources.authority: Primary documentation for OpenAI developer products
sources.license_reuse: Link to canonical pages and follow site terms; do not redistribute documentation wholesale.
sources.known_gaps: Product-specific and fast-moving; re-check current APIs, model behavior, pricing, and limits before use.

sources.title: OpenAI Cookbook
sources.authority: Official example collection supporting OpenAI developer workflows
sources.license_reuse: Link to canonical examples and verify the repository license and individual dependencies before reuse.
sources.known_gaps: Examples illustrate patterns but are not guarantees of production fitness or comprehensive safety coverage.

concepts.outcome: Write, trace, test, and debug small Python programs.
Use arrays, shapes, indexing, broadcasting, and vectorization safely.
Use version control and deterministic tests to run reproducible exercises.
Reason about processes, memory, CPU/GPU execution, and bottlenecks.
Read, validate, transform, and query common data formats.
Translate vector and matrix operations among geometry, algebra, and code.
Derive gradients with the chain rule and verify them numerically or with autodiff.
Model conditional uncertainty with random variables, expectation, and Bayes rule.
Reason about samples, estimators, uncertainty, bias, variance, and leakage.
Explain and apply gradient optimization, regularization, and conditioning trade-offs.
Use entropy, cross-entropy, and KL divergence to interpret learning objectives.
Implement and compare uninformed, heuristic, and adversarial search under explicit cost and correctness constraints.
Represent and solve constraint or planning problems while explaining heuristics, failure cases, and computational trade-offs.
Represent uncertain or symbolic knowledge and perform defensible inference while stating assumptions and limits.
Model a sequential decision problem and implement or evaluate value, policy, and learning methods without hiding reward or exploration assumptions.
Translate a real goal into targets, constraints, baselines, and falsifiable success criteria.
Audit provenance, licensing, missingness, sampling, imbalance, and leakage.
Design reproducible offline or online experiments with valid comparisons.
Choose metrics, quantify uncertainty, calibrate predictions, and analyze failure slices.
Fit and interpret regularized linear and logistic models.
Choose and tune trees, random forests, and boosting while explaining bias and variance.
Explain similarity-based prediction and select kernels or neighborhoods under constraints.
Apply clustering, PCA, and anomaly detection without overstating conclusions.
Build a leakage-resistant preprocessing, validation, selection, and evaluation pipeline.
Deploy and monitor a versioned machine-learning service with reproducible features, drift checks, rollback, and explicit cost and reliability limits.
Trace tensors through forward and backward passes and diagnose gradient errors.
Train and stabilize MLPs using initialization, normalization, regularization, and optimizers.
Explain spatial inductive bias and implement a compact convolutional model.
Explain recurrence and sequence bottlenecks as context for attention.
Compute and interpret attention, masking, heads, and tensor shapes.
Explain and test vocabulary, segmentation, normalization, and token-cost trade-offs.
Trace a causal transformer block from token IDs to next-token logits.
Reason about objectives, data, contamination, compute, scaling, and evidence limits.
Choose and evaluate decoding strategies under quality, diversity, and latency constraints.
Compare fine-tuning, adapters, instruction tuning, and preference optimization with appropriate evaluation.
Reason about KV cache, quantization, batching, throughput, latency, and memory trade-offs.
Design prompts and validate structured outputs against schemas and failure cases.
Build and evaluate chunking, indexing, retrieval, reranking, grounding, and citations.
Build deterministic tool-using workflows with typed boundaries and recovery paths.
Choose agentic versus fixed workflows and design state, memory, permissions, and human approval.
Design and evaluate a multimodal pipeline when the target needs it.
Create representative eval sets, rubrics, graders, confidence estimates, and release gates.
Threat-model prompt injection, data exfiltration, unsafe execution, and authorization failures.
Analyze fairness, privacy, consent, provenance, transparency, copyright, and misuse trade-offs.
Operate a versioned service with cost, latency, observability, fallback, rollback, and incident constraints.
Separate a paper's claims, assumptions, method, evidence, limitations, and speculation.
Reproduce a scoped result and design baselines, ablations, sensitivity tests, and negative controls.
Build and defend an end-to-end system or research result, including limitations and next experiments.
